meta.titre: Methods of Payment: from cash to cheques and transfers
meta.sous_theme: Cash, cheques, standing orders and other ways of settling a debt

sections.contenu_markdown: At the end of the month a shopkeeper in Douala must pay her landlord, her electricity bill, her supplier and her shop assistant. She could carry banknotes to each of them, but cash can be lost or stolen and is hard to prove. Modern traders use cheques, transfers, standing orders and mobile money instead. The GCE Commerce papers ask you to match a method of payment to a situation, to distinguish open from crossed cheques and to explain why a cheque may be refused. This course shows you how.

items: A debtor is a person who owes money; a creditor is a person who is owed money.
A bank account holder can instruct the bank to pay money to someone else.
Money is a medium of exchange accepted in payment for goods and services.

sections.titre: Ways of settling a debt and how to choose between them
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Main methods of payment

| Method | How it works | Best for |
|---|---|---|
| Cash | Notes and coins handed over | Small, immediate purchases |
| Cheque | A written order to the drawer's bank to pay a named payee | Payments between businesses; a record exists |
| Bank draft | A cheque issued by the bank itself, paid for in advance by the buyer | Large or one-off payments to a seller who does not trust a cheque |
| Standing order | The bank pays a **fixed** amount to the same person at **regular** dates | Rent, loan repayments, subscriptions |
| Direct debit | The creditor collects **varying** amounts from the account with the debtor's permission | Bills that change from month to month |
| Credit transfer | The bank moves money directly from one account to another | Salaries, payments to suppliers |
| Card | Debit or credit card used at a till, machine or online | Shopping and cash withdrawals |
| Mobile money | Money moved by phone between accounts held with a mobile service | Small payments and transfers by people without bank accounts |

### The cheque

The **drawer** writes the cheque, the **drawee** is the bank on which it is drawn and the **payee** is the person to be paid. The amount in words must agree with the amount in figures. The cheque must be signed, dated and not altered without the drawer's initials.

### Choosing a method

Ask: is the amount fixed or does it change? Is it regular or one-off? How much trust is there between the two parties? How fast must the money arrive? How safe is the method?

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question asks you to distinguish between the two
variantes.contenu_markdown: An **open cheque** carries no crossing: the payee can present it at the drawer's bank and receive cash across the counter, so it is risky if lost. A **crossed cheque** has two parallel lines drawn across its face: it must be paid into a bank account and cannot be cashed over the counter, so a thief finds it harder to use. In a **special crossing** the name of a bank is written between the lines, and the cheque must go through that bank.

variantes.nom: Why a cheque may be dishonoured
variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question asks for reasons a bank refuses to pay
variantes.contenu_markdown: Any four: there is not enough money in the drawer's account; the signature is missing or does not match the specimen; the words and the figures disagree; the cheque has been altered without the drawer's signature; it is post-dated (the date has not yet arrived); it is too old (stale); the drawer has stopped the payment; or the drawer's account has been closed.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question gives a bill and asks for the right instruction to the bank
variantes.contenu_markdown: Use a **standing order** when the amount and the date are fixed, such as rent. Use a **direct debit** when the amount varies and the creditor collects it, such as a utility bill. The customer gives the instruction in both cases, but the first is started by the payer and the second by the creditor.

sections.enonce_markdown: The bursar of a school has to settle these payments: (i) a rent of 250,000 FCFA on the same day every month; (ii) a water bill that changes every month; (iii) a large one-off payment to a new supplier who does not accept a cheque from a customer he does not yet know. Advise the bursar on a method of payment for each and give one reason.

etapes.justification: Look at the amount (fixed or changing), the rhythm (regular or one-off) and the trust between the parties.
etapes.resultat_markdown: (i) fixed and regular; (ii) varying and regular; (iii) large, one-off, low trust.

etapes.justification: A fixed amount at regular dates is exactly what a standing order does, and it avoids late payment.
etapes.resultat_markdown: **Standing order.** Over a year it moves 3,000,000 FCFA in twelve equal payments: $12 \times 250\,000 = 3\,000\,000$ FCFA.

etapes.justification: The amount changes each month, so a fixed instruction would be wrong. A direct debit lets the creditor collect the right amount, or the bursar can pay by cheque or transfer when the bill arrives.
etapes.resultat_markdown: **Direct debit** (or a cheque on receipt of each bill).

etapes.justification: A bank draft is issued by the bank itself and paid for in advance, so the seller is sure the money exists.

sections.conclusion_markdown: The bursar should use a **standing order** for the rent, a **direct debit** for the changing water bill and a **bank draft** for the new supplier. Each method is chosen because it matches the amount, the regularity and the trust involved. The standing order also gives the school a record of 3,000,000 FCFA paid in rent each year.

items.erreur_markdown: 'A crossed cheque cannot be paid at all.'
items.pourquoi_faux: It can be paid, but only into a bank account, not as cash across the counter.
items.correction_markdown: A crossed cheque is paid into the payee's bank account. It cannot be cashed at the counter.

items.erreur_markdown: 'A standing order is used to pay an electricity bill that changes each month.'
items.pourquoi_faux: A standing order has a fixed amount. A bill whose amount changes needs a direct debit or a payment by cheque or transfer each time.
items.correction_markdown: Standing order: fixed amount, regular dates. Direct debit: variable amount collected by the creditor.

items.erreur_markdown: 'A bank draft can bounce for lack of funds like a cheque.'
items.pourquoi_faux: The bank issues the draft after taking the money from the buyer, so there is no risk that the drawer's account is empty. That is why sellers trust it.
items.correction_markdown: A bank draft is guaranteed by the bank that issues it.

items.erreur_markdown: 'If the words and the figures on a cheque differ, the bank pays the larger amount.'
items.pourquoi_faux: The bank will normally return the cheque because it cannot tell which amount the drawer meant.
items.correction_markdown: Make the amount in words and the amount in figures agree before signing.

items.erreur_markdown: Mixing up the drawer and the payee
items.pourquoi_faux: The drawer writes and signs the cheque; the payee receives the money.
items.correction_markdown: Drawer: the person who writes the cheque. Payee: the person named to receive the money. Drawee: the bank.

items.enonce_markdown: Mr Fon writes a cheque for 30,000 FCFA and names Mrs Eba as the person to receive the money. His account is held at a commercial bank. Identify the drawer, the payee and the drawee.
items.solution_markdown: The **drawer** is Mr Fon, because he writes and signs the cheque. The **payee** is Mrs Eba, who receives the money. The **drawee** is the commercial bank where Mr Fon's account is held.

items.enonce_markdown: Choose the most suitable method of payment for each situation and give a reason: (a) a monthly loan repayment of 75,000 FCFA that is the same each month; (b) a small purchase of fruit at a market stall; (c) a company paying the monthly salaries of 40 workers; (d) a telephone bill whose amount changes each month. Also calculate the total repaid in a year under (a).
items.solution_markdown:
(a) **Standing order**: fixed amount at regular dates. Total in a year: $12 \times 75\,000 = 900\,000$ FCFA, that is **900,000 FCFA**.

(b) **Cash** (or mobile money): small and immediate.

(c) **Credit transfer**: the bank pays many people from one instruction and keeps a record.

(d) **Direct debit**: the creditor collects the changing amount.

items.enonce_markdown: A supplier is asked to accept a cheque of 1,350,000 FCFA from a customer he has never met. (a) Give three reasons why the supplier may hesitate. (b) Suggest two safer ways for the customer to pay. (c) Suppose the bank charges a fee of 0.5% of the amount for a bank draft of this sum. Calculate the fee and the total cost to the customer.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) Any three: the cheque may be dishonoured for lack of funds; the signature may not match; the cheque may be post-dated or stale; the drawer may stop the payment; there is a delay before the money is cleared.

(b) Any two: a **bank draft**, a **credit transfer**, or payment in **cash** on delivery.

(c) Fee $= \frac{0.5}{100} \times 1\,350\,000 = 6\,750$ FCFA. Total cost $= 1\,350\,000 + 6\,750 = 1\,356\,750$ FCFA. **Fee: 6,750 FCFA; total: 1,356,750 FCFA.**

items_markdown: Cash is quick but unsafe; a cheque is a written order to pay; a bank draft is guaranteed by the bank; a standing order pays a fixed amount regularly; a direct debit collects varying amounts.
Drawer writes the cheque, drawee is the bank, payee receives the money.
An open cheque can be cashed at the counter; a crossed cheque must be paid into a bank account.
A cheque may be dishonoured for insufficient funds, a missing or wrong signature, words and figures that disagree, alterations, a post-dated or stale date, or a stopped payment.
Match the method to the payment: fixed and regular (standing order), varying (direct debit), large one-off (bank draft), many salaries (credit transfer).
Mobile money and cards are modern methods that suit small and everyday payments.
